public_health_question.v: What were the characteristics, sexual behaviors and strain features of a Shigella sonnei outbreak among men who have sex with men in San Francisco in 2000-2001?

ev.q: This report describes an investigation of S. sonnei cases that occurred among MSM in San Francisco during May--December 2000.
Shigella sonnei Outbreak Among Men Who Have Sex with Men --- San Francisco, California, 2000--2001
This report describes an investigation of S. sonnei cases that occurred among MSM in San Francisco during May--December 2000.
230 cases of culture-confirmed* S. sonnei infection were reported to the San Francisco Department of Public Health
106 were selected randomly for telephone interview; 35 (33%) could not be contacted and four (4%) refused to participate.
San Francisco, California, 2000--2001

equity.level_reason: Rates for MSM (259/100,000) and all other groups (16) are set side by side with no computed ratio, and MSM is framed as a risk group; race, education, income and insurance are respondent descriptors only.

level_alternative.reason: MSM may be read as a transmission or behavioral risk category rather than a SOGI social position, leaving race and SES as descriptors only.

equity.equity_measurement: MSM rate uses denominators from the San Francisco HIV/AIDS epidemiology report; the referent lumps women and heterosexual men; sexual behavior unknown for 31% of cases.

notes: No tests or CIs; contrasts (MSM vs other rates, 230 cases vs a 1996-1999 average of 21, outbreak vs control PFGE patterns, HIV share vs cited 20% prevalence) are side by side. PFGE subtyping and susceptibility testing characterize isolates and are not recorded as procedures.
